title: DACS-3 §8.5.2 negotiable price-band bounds: exact half-up rounding, inclusive boundaries, CD-1 canonical refusal

clauses.DACS-3 §8.5.2 (negotiable pricing): The admissible band is the inclusive interval [bandCenter.amount × (100 − minPct) / 100, bandCenter.amount × (100 + maxPct) / 100]. Each computed bound MUST be rounded half-up to the number of fractional digits of bandCenter.amount in its CD-1 canonical form (CORE §B.2) — NOT to any "currency precision" — then canonicalised per CD-1. terms.price.amount, compared as a full-precision CD-1 decimal, MUST be ≥ the lower bound and ≤ the upper bound (boundaries inclusive). A verifier MUST reject the listing if the computed lower bound is ≤ 0. minPct / maxPct are non-negative percentages.
clauses.CORE §B.2 (rule CD-1): Every PriceTerm.amount string MUST be in minimal-digit canonical decimal form: no leading zeros (except a single 0 before the decimal point); no trailing zeros after the decimal point; . as the only separator; no + sign; no exponent. Verifiers MUST canonicalise amount per CD-1 before any price-band or price-equality comparison.

derivation: Expected bounds were computed independently from the quoted clause with arbitrary-precision decimal arithmetic (Python decimal, ROUND_HALF_UP, quantized to the fractional digits of the canonical band centre, then CD-1-canonicalised). No expected value was copied from SDK output.

offerExpectations.refused-noncanonical: the amount violates CD-1, so the comparison MUST be refused rather than normalised (CORE §B.2)
offerExpectations.refused-zero: SDK declared contract, labeled as such: a zero amount (CD-1 canonical but never a valid positive price) is refused before comparison — an additional SDK guard, not a quoted-clause derivation

vectors.name: half-up-one-fractional-digit
vectors.cite: DACS-3 §8.5.2: bounds rounded half-up to the fractional digits of the CD-1 band centre; boundaries inclusive
vectors.note: raw bounds 1.35 / 1.65; one fractional digit (centre 1.5) rounds both half-up to 1.4 / 1.7. The raw lower bound 1.35 is itself OUTSIDE the rounded band.

vectors.name: zero-amount-comparison-refused-sdk-contract
vectors.cite: SDK declared contract (labeled, NOT a quoted-clause derivation): isNegotiablePriceWithinBand refuses a zero amount before any band comparison. Zero is CD-1 canonical, so CORE §B.2 does not require this refusal; it is the SDK's own guard, consistent with DACS-3 §8.5.2's requirement that a valid band be strictly positive

vectors.name: integer-centre-half-up-asymmetry
vectors.cite: DACS-3 §8.5.2: zero fractional digits in the centre means integer bounds; half-up pulls the lower midpoint UP into the band's exterior and the upper midpoint UP into the band
vectors.note: centre 15 ±10%: raw 13.5 / 16.5. Half-up gives 14 / 17 — so 13.5 is outside (lower rounded away from it) while 16.5 is within (upper rounded past it). This asymmetry is the observable signature of half-up.

vectors.name: exact-midpoint-both-bounds
vectors.cite: DACS-3 §8.5.2: each computed bound rounded half-up to the centre's fractional digits (two digits here)
vectors.note: centre 0.01 ±50%: raw 0.005 / 0.015 are both exact midpoints at two fractional digits; half-up gives 0.01 / 0.02 (lower rounds back onto the centre).

vectors.name: upper-bound-cd1-canonicalisation
vectors.cite: DACS-3 §8.5.2: bounds are rounded, then canonicalised per CD-1 (CORE §B.2: no trailing zeros)
vectors.note: centre 2.4, minPct 0, maxPct 25: raw upper 3.0 at one fractional digit MUST surface as CD-1 canonical "3", never "3.0". An offer spelled "3.0" is refused as noncanonical even though its value is in band.

vectors.name: fractional-percentage-exact
vectors.cite: DACS-3 §8.5.2: minPct/maxPct are percentages (JSON numbers); 12.5% of 8 is exact, no rounding effect

vectors.name: wide-asymmetric-integer-band
vectors.cite: DACS-3 §8.5.2: asymmetric minPct/maxPct; raw lower 3.5 rounds half-up to 4 at zero fractional digits

vectors.name: noncanonical-centre-refused
vectors.cite: CORE §B.2 CD-1: no trailing zeros after the decimal point; a noncanonical band centre MUST be refused, not silently normalised

vectors.name: zero-centre-refused
vectors.cite: DACS-3 §8.5.2: a computed lower bound ≤ 0 MUST be rejected; a zero centre cannot produce a positive band

vectors.name: min-pct-100-refused
vectors.cite: DACS-3 §8.5.2: lower bound = centre × (100 − 100) / 100 = 0; a verifier MUST reject a computed lower bound ≤ 0

vectors.name: rounded-lower-bound-zero-refused
vectors.cite: DACS-3 §8.5.2: the REJECTED quantity is the computed (rounded) lower bound; centre 0.4 − 99% = raw 0.004, half-up at one fractional digit = 0.0 ≤ 0

vectors.name: negative-min-pct-refused
vectors.cite: DACS-3 §8.5.2: minPct / maxPct are non-negative percentages; a negative percentage MUST be refused
